PerformanceTroubleshooting.Title: Check Performance Issues
PerformanceTroubleshooting.Description: LENET procedure when EVERYTHING is slow on a computer (not just mail, one app, or internet).

Sections.Title: 1 - Spec Recommendation
Sections.Description: If the computer is below recommendations, the issue may be hardware. If above ALL specs, proceed to troubleshooting.

Steps.Title: Check hardware against LENET spec recommendations
Steps.Instructions: Review SSD/HDD, CPU, RAM, and workstation age. Inform user if HDD or under-spec.

Steps.Title: Verify storage in ConnectWise Automate (CWA)
Steps.Instructions: CWA > Storage tile > Media Type. SSD = Good. HDD or Other (confirm model) = performance bottleneck. Inform user they should upgrade to SSD.

Steps.Title: CPU benchmark lookup
Steps.Instructions: Search CPU at https://www.cpubenchmark.net/cpu_list.php — Score < 4000 = bad, > 4000 = okay, > 5000 = very good.

Steps.Title: Warranty / age decision
Steps.Instructions: < 1 year: run troubleshooting, warranty may apply if steps fail. 1-3 years: consult support leader/account manager if we sold it. > 4 years: recommend replacement (2021+ spec requirements).

Steps.Title: CPU & Memory snapshot
Steps.Instructions: If consistently > 90%, investigate top processes. Chrome with many tabs, high svchost = patch/driver issue.

Steps.Title: Open Resource Monitor
Steps.Instructions: Review CPU, Memory, Disk tabs. Kill problematic process as temp fix; apply patches for svchost issues.

Steps.Title: Top CPU & memory processes
Steps.Instructions: Identify resource hogs. Try driver updates and Windows Update before Patch My PC.

Sections.Title: 2 - Tools to Speed Up & Fix Issues

Steps.Title: ScreenConnect Backstage (optional)
Steps.Instructions: Right-click workstation > Join with Options > Join backstageCalls > Join session. Backstage runs as SYSTEM (admin). Use for remote work without bothering the client.

Steps.Title: SFC and DISM scan (full sequence)
Steps.Instructions: Run in CMD or Backstage. Screenshot results of every command.

Steps.Title: System File Checker (SFC)
Steps.Instructions: Run after DISM sequence completes.

Steps.Title: Driver updates in CWA
Steps.Instructions: Tiles > Patching > filter Category to Drivers. Keywords: firmware, system component, Extension, AMD/Intel, network, audio. Install one-by-one; check Jobs menu for success. Ask user to restart in 1-2 hours.

Steps.Title: Manufacturer support & driver tools
Steps.Instructions: Serial from ScreenConnect General section. Run HP Support Assistant, Dell Command Update, or Lenovo System Update. Ask senior/SOC leader before network or BIOS updates.

Steps.Title: Patch My PC
Steps.Instructions: Run available software updates from Patch My PC.

Steps.Title: Audit startup applications
Steps.Instructions: Disable unnecessary startup apps. Do NOT disable Adobe, driver services (Broadcom, Realtek, Intel, AD), or LENET services. Ask senior if unsure.

Steps.Title: Audit non-Microsoft services
Steps.Instructions: Win+R > msconfig > Services. Disable unnecessary non-Microsoft services with same exclusions as startup.

Steps.Title: Clear user temp folder (%temp%)
Steps.Instructions: Select all (Ctrl+A), delete. Skip files requiring admin. Check 'Do this for all current items'.

Steps.Title: Disk cleanup
Steps.Instructions: Also consider WinDirStat for storage analysis. IMUSA: see ITB KB for additional cleanup.

Steps.Title: Clear system temp files
Steps.Instructions: Removes aged temp files from system locations.

Sections.Title: 3 - Slow Startup (perf OK but slow boot)

Steps.Title: Check disk free space
Steps.Instructions: Less than 20% free can cause slow startup. Follow disk cleanup if low.

Steps.Title: Recent Windows updates installed
Steps.Instructions: Cross-reference with CWA: Tiles > Patching > History. Filter Failed/In Progress around incident date. Consider uninstalling problematic KB/driver.

Steps.Title: CWA patching history
Steps.Instructions: ConnectWise Automate > ComputerName > Tiles > Patching > History. Filter Failed/In Progress for dates around when issue started.

Steps.Title: Check ImmyBot failed sessions
Steps.Instructions: ImmyBot > Sessions > filter Failed + date range + computer name. Review failed action and error. Check C:\ProgramData\ImmyBot\Logs on workstation if needed.

Steps.Title: Process Explorer
Steps.Instructions: Toolbox Level 1 or download Sysinternals. Sort by Working Set for memory. Options > Configure Colors (dark purple = investigate). Right-click > Properties for autostart location. Can run in Backstage.
